transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-07
Start time (UTC): 14:30
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Reyes (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (CTO, Pegasus Pay), Priya Nair (Head of ML), Ethan Park (SRE)

Summary: Integration discovery for embedding Redwood into Pegasus Pay's fraud-detection pipeline. Focus: SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex integrations, gateway/proxy setup, rate limits/quotas, and observability hooks for alerts and tracing.

Topics: SDKs & examples; LangChain / LlamaIndex connectors; private gateway vs direct API; rate-limits and quotas per route; observability (tracing, logs, token-level cost breakdown); Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs for throughput and isolation.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE on the account, and Carlos is our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Liam O'Connor: Good, thanks. Quick note, we've got about 45 minutes. Want to make sure we cover integration details — Priya is most interested in the LangChain flow.
[00:12] Priya Nair: Yep, hi. We're evaluating Redwood for a couple of use cases: real-time fraud detection in payments and an internal compliance assistant. Main asks: how quickly can we wire this up, and what are the constraints on latency and throughput?
[00:22] Carlos Reyes: Great, thanks. Quick high-level — Redwood offers Hosted API and Dedicated reserved capacity; there's also Private (VPC/on-prem) for strict data residency. For integrations we have official SDKs (Python/Node), and we provide connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex.
[00:33] Priya Nair: Are those connectors maintained by Redwood or community? We rely on LlamaIndex heavily.
[00:38] Carlos Reyes: We maintain official adapters and examples for both; we also ship a few reference notebooks that show LlamaIndex pipelines with chunking, embeddings calls, and caching. The LangChain adapter supports chain-of-thought prompts and function/tool calling patterns — it's in our SDK repo.
[00:49] Ethan Park: From infra side: do you expect us to call the Redwood hosted endpoint directly from our services, or do you recommend a gateway/proxy in front? We have strict IP allowlists and want to limit egress.
[00:58] Maya Chen: Good question. Many customers put a lightweight gateway or proxy in front  — either an internal API gateway or a dedicated proxy  — for IP allowlisting, authentication, and request shaping. Redwood's Hosted supports IP allowlisting and VPC peering for Private, but a proxy gives you extra control over retries and per-route rate limiting.
[01:12] Liam O'Connor: If we go Hosted, how do we handle credential rotation and KMS? We're paranoid about keys in services that touch PII.
[01:18] Carlos Reyes: Hosted supports short-lived tokens and integrates with customer SSO for admin UI access. For encryption at rest and key management, we support bringing your own keys via KMS for Private deployments; for Hosted we use provider-managed KMS but can provide SOC2 artifacts. We'll share the security whitepaper.
[01:30] Priya Nair: On quotas/rate limits: our fraud model needs to do many short generation calls — bearer checks — plus embedding lookups. How granular are rate limits? Can we set per-route and per-model quotas?
[01:40] Maya Chen: Yes. Redwood supports token- and request-based quotas. On Hosted you can get per-api-key rate limits and per-route quotas (we can set different limits for embeddings vs. completion endpoints). With Dedicated you get capacity isolation — predictable throughput and ability to configure autoscale policies.
[01:52] Priya Nair: Any idea of headroom — like how many qps per GPU or per Dedicated unit?
[01:58] Carlos Reyes: That depends on model and sequence length. For a typical open smaller model used for reranking/embeddings we can get hundreds of QPS with batching; for low-latency generation at 100-token responses, SLOs vary. We'll propose a benchmark plan — if you can share sample payload sizes and concurrency, we can map to Dedicated pool sizes.
[02:15] Ethan Park: We'll send sample traffic. Also, observability is huge for us: traces correlated with token costs, per-call latency, and per-route dashboards. Does Redwood expose tracing hooks?
[02:25] Carlos Reyes: Yes — our Console exposes token-level cost breakdown, per-model and per-route latency histograms, and error rates. For deeper integration, we provide a tracing hook and can emit structured logs to your logging endpoint (gzipped JSON). We also support OTLP for traces and have an ingestion hook to append request_id from your side so you can correlate.
[02:43] Liam O'Connor: Does that require Dedicated or is that available on Hosted too?
[02:47] Maya Chen: Observability features are on Hosted as well; Dedicated and Private give extended retention and extra tracing bandwidth options. For example, Dedicated customers can push higher-resolution traces and increase telemetry retention windows.
[02:58] Priya Nair: About LangChain/LlamaIndex — do you have examples of prompt caching or prefix caching? We're worried about repeated prompts and token costs.
[03:06] Carlos Reyes: We have prefix/KV cache examples and an SDK layer that supports automatic prefix caching and deduplication. On Dedicated we can enable a shared cache in the serving runtime to reduce repeated computation. Also the SDK supports client-side caching with TTLs.
[03:19] Priya Nair: That might be enough to get costs down for fraud checks. On billing — do you do per-token only or per-request tiers?
[03:26] Maya Chen: Hosted is usage-based (per-token/per-embedding), plus optional observability add-ons. Dedicated is reserved capacity (monthly commit) with a base platform fee and usage tiers for bursts. We can send a draft pricing sheet.
[03:36] Ethan Park: For security review — do you have SOC2 and pen test reports? We'll need those for procurement.
[03:41] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll share SOC2 Type II, basic pen test summary, and our data flow diagram. We'll include notes on KMS and HSM integrations.
[03:49] Liam O'Connor: Ok, technical nit: we use LlamaIndex to build vector stores backed by our internal PG vector DB. Are there recommended patterns for embedding calls and connector code? We don't want to leak vectors externally.
[03:59] Carlos Reyes: Recommended pattern: do embeddings in your own VPC if you're highly sensitive (Private deployment), or use Hosted with strict retention policies and tokenization controls. Our SDK has examples that show embedding batching, chunking strategy, and how to substitute your vector store calls so vectors never leave your private environment. We'll attach LlamaIndex example notebook.
[04:17] Priya Nair: Latency expectations for synchronous fraud checks — we need <200ms ideally for the model call path. Is that realistic?
[04:23] Carlos Reyes: For small embedding lookups and lightweight model calls, 100-200ms can be achieved with Dedicated and tuned batching turned off for those routes. Hosted can get close in our fastest regions but Dedicated gives SLO guarantees. We'll document specifics after we see payload sizes.
[04:36] Maya Chen: To summarize, sounds like immediate steps: we share SDK quickstarts, LangChain/LlamaIndex examples, SOC2/security docs, and a benchmark plan. Carlos will coordinate a benchmark run if Pegasus can provide an AWS test account or a replay of traffic.
[04:49] Liam O'Connor: That works. Procurement will want Dedicated pricing and SLA.
[04:52] Maya Chen: We'll draft Dedicated pricing and SLA options. Any blockers from your side?
[04:56] Priya Nair: None beyond us sharing traffic shapes and providing an infra contact for the benchmark.
[05:00] Ethan Park: I'll provide sample flow and a staging account.
[05:03] Maya Chen: Perfect. Quick clarifying Q — Priya, for the LlamaIndex connector do you want us to show a pattern where embeddings are computed in your VPC and only indexes are used in Redwood, or to show a Hosted flow?
[05:12] Priya Nair: Show both if possible, but emphasize the VPC/private embedding pattern.
[05:16] Carlos Reyes: Noted. We'll include both in the examples and flag security tradeoffs.
[05:21] Maya Chen: Anything else on quotas or routing?
[05:24] Liam O'Connor: One more — can we do model fallbacks? If a pinned model is overloaded can Redwood route to a cheaper variant automatically?
[05:30] Carlos Reyes: Yes, smart routing supports fallback policies by model variant, region, or capacity tier. You can configure latency-first or cost-first routing. We'll include a config snippet.
[05:39] Maya Chen: Ok closing recap: next steps — Maya to send SDK + LangChain/LlamaIndex examples and SOC2/security docs; Carlos to draft benchmark plan and request sample traffic details; Pegasus to share sample traffic and a staging account. We'll also send draft Dedicated pricing and SLA.
[05:54] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good. Thanks, everyone.
[05:57] Priya Nair: Thanks.
[05:58] End of recording.

Notes: Transcript contains a few transcription errors and some speaker label switches in the raw capture. References to specific internal Redwood product names (e.g., Console, Dedicated) may be slightly garbled in auto-transcription but were clarified during the call.
